item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 4, 2026
item.description:
With the latest from across the media business, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
Building a successful radio station takes more than great music and personalities. In a new Media Jobs Report blog, Brian Wright of Wright Media Group shares 10 key principles learned over more than 40 years in broadcasting. From positioning and programming to marketing, leadership and listener loyalty, Wright explains why a winning strategy means nothing without consistent execution. Read his insights at Media Jobs Report dot com.
Turning to technology,
The Local Media Association and Google News Initiative have selected 12 newsrooms for their six-month AI Growth Lab. Participants include AFRO News, Appen Media Group, Carolina Panorama Newspaper, Gallup Sun Publishing, Greenfield Recorder, Salem Reporter, The Atlanta Voice, The Colorado Sun, The Columbian, The New York Amsterdam News, The Santa Fe New Mexican, and The Seattle Times. The program will help publishers use artificial intelligence to improve efficiency, grow audiences and increase revenue.
In television news,
Gray Media has promoted Jaime Eskridge to General Manager of WLFI-TV, its CBS affiliate in Lafayette, Indiana. Eskridge joined the station in 2015 and later worked on Allen Media’s corporate digital team, supporting 22 television stations. She returned to WLFI late last year and has served as Interim General Manager for several months. Her promotion took effect November second.
Turning to radio,
Audacy has added Nikki Preston to the morning show at Kiss 98.5 in Buffalo. Preston joins Nicholas Picholas and Wease weekdays from 6 to 10. A Rochester native, Preston returns to Western New York after more than a decade in Southern California radio, including stops at ALT 94.9 in San Diego and 96.7 KCAL Rocks.
In media technology news,
The National Association of Broadcasters is accepting nominations for its 2027 Technology Awards, recognizing excellence in radio and television engineering, digital leadership, and technology innovation. Nominations for the Digital Leadership and Engineering Achievement Awards close January 19th, while the Technology Innovation Award deadline is March 1st. Winners will be honored at NAB Show in Las Vegas this April.
Turning to technology,
Adobe is teaming up with Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group to bring licensed music directly into Premiere mobile. The free video-editing app will soon let creators search popular songs, add up to 60 seconds of music, and build videos using customizable templates. Tracks will be available for personal, non-commercial use, giving artists and songwriters new opportunities to reach audiences through social media.
And finally,
Michael Courier is back in his home state of Michigan, joining TEGNA’s WZZM-TV in Grand Rapids as Weekend Morning Anchor and Weekday Morning Reporter. The Bay City native spent more than four years in Texas, working at KVIA in El Paso and KVUE in Austin. Courier made his WZZM anchoring debut October 24.
For more industry news, the latest media jobs and free tools, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
